newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil futures close lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil futures close lower on fund selling.

text.p: Fund selling drove CBOT soyoil futures to a lower close but scale-down commercial demand limited the losses, traders said.
"Oil and wheat weighed on everything and there was talk China bought oil from South America," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Funds sold from 1,500 to 2,000 lots of soyoil on the day and Griffin Trading sold at least 1,000 lots. Commercials countered with ADM Investor Services purchasing 600 lots of January while Continental Grain bought 150 lots of March and Produce Grain bought 150 lots of January, traders said.
Traders said the commercial buying was expected as January broke support at the 23-cent-per-lb mark.
"Funds were selling oil and broke 23 in the January and it spilled into beans," a trader said.
Fundamentals were little changed with near-ideal crop weather in South America continuing to weigh on prices, the traders said.
